title: GPT-6 Astra assists a gauge-invariant lattice chiral-fermion measure construction
summary: Nathaniel Craig proposes a smooth, exponentially local, gauge-invariant fermion measure on admissible four-dimensional lattices, with restrictions covering the Standard Model gauge groups. GPT-6 Astra helped develop the refinement construction and led the detailed proof. The supplementary report states that Lean kernel replay accepted the encoded measure-existence result and supporting inputs under their recorded assumptions. This is a candidate finite-lattice definition; reflection positivity, practical simulation and an interacting continuum theory remain outside the established claim. The October 6, 2026 preprint preceded the November 15 institutional announcement.
organization: University of California, Santa Barbara; OpenAI

evidence.tested: Source-reported Lean kernel replay checked the concrete companion measure-existence theorem, its analytic/geometric inputs and Standard Model restrictions under encoded definitions and assumptions. Same-study mathematical and two-dimensional computational checks are also reported.
evidence.unknown: Review checked the preprint verification/conclusion sections and formal-verification supplement, not an independently executed Lean build. Formal-to-source correspondence was reviewed by AI agents. A separate frozen-reference comparator failed on generated proof names; the report distinguishes this from successful kernel replay. Kernel correctness is relative to the encoded claim and axioms; it does not establish reflection positivity, a physical continuum limit, independent scientific confirmation or practical usefulness.
evidence.ai_role: Craig supplied the refinement strategy; Astra developed key construction steps, led proof development and carried out proposed verification work.
